_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY — this file is documentation, not a live manifest. cImp never
reads it: the updater fetches the pinned URL in
src-tauri/src/offload/detection/updater/manifest.rs::DEFAULT_MANIFEST_URL
(https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dyserna/cImp/detection-v1/manifest.json).
It is committed so the schema has a worked example next to the data it
describes, and so the first real publish is a copy-edit rather than a
design step.
THE CHANNEL IS A BRANCH, NOT A RELEASE (changed 2026-08-08, #48 H-5).
It pointed at a release-asset URL until then. GitHub answers EVERY
release-asset path with a 302 to a signed CDN host, and the fetcher refuses
redirects on purpose (the U-1 hardening). Publishing under that design would
have produced a channel that never updated on any install and stayed silent
about it for a week. raw.githubusercontent.com answers 200 directly, so the
redirect ban stays intact, and a ~19 KB text bundle belongs in a git tree
anyway: diffable, reviewable, and published by a commit instead of an asset
upload with a flat namespace to work around.
DEPLOY (V32 Phase C3 — nothing updates until these are done):
1. Create an orphan branch `detection-v1` on Dyserna/cImp holding ONLY the
channel files (manifest.json + the versioned .yar files). Orphan, so
the channel's history is not the app's and a clone of it is tiny. Fixed
ref, contents updated over time — never a moving 'latest' pointer: the
pinned URL is what makes the channel curated.
2. Curate the first bundle from detection/rules.d/*.yar (the shipped seed)
plus whatever the current maintenance run pulled from the garak corpus.
(Vigil is dormant — last push 2024-01-31 — so it is a source of rule
SHAPES, not of refreshes.) Version it as a DATE (e.g. 2026.08.08) —
the rule bundle is not semver.
3. Verify the candidate locally before publishing: point
offload.detection_update_manifest_url at a local http server serving
a staged copy and confirm the run reports `applied`. That exercises the
same gauntlet the channel will face, including the smoke corpus in
detection/smoke/ and the coverage floor.
NOTE what this step CANNOT catch: a local server answers 200, so it
never exercises the transport property that H-5 turned on. Before the
first real publish, also point the setting at a THROWAWAY ref on the
real host and confirm one live run.
4. Commit the .yar files to the branch. Names must be unique across
versions (a branch keeps every version's files side by side), hence the
`<version>-<file>` convention in the URLs below.
5. Write manifest.json with the real sha256 (sha256sum) and byte sizes,
and push it LAST — a manifest published before its files makes every
install fail a check it would otherwise have skipped. Two commits, or
one commit that adds files and one that adds the manifest.
6. Set min_app_version only when a bundle actually needs a newer app
(e.g. a rule using a yara-x feature an older build cannot compile).
There is exactly ONE component: `rules`. A `classifier` component existed
until 2026-08-08 and was removed. The Prompt Guard 2 weights are HF-gated,
a released checkpoint has no update stream, and locked decision 7 already
ships them through the models-v1 release-asset pipeline with CHECKSUMS.txt
— the same path as the TTS and STT blobs, at maintenance-run cadence. Users
either take the release that bundles the models or fetch them themselves.
A manifest that still lists `classifier` is not an error: the parser's
forward-compatible skip ignores any component this build does not know.

components.notes: Seed bundle: 19 rules across the instruction-override, role-forgery, guardrail-removal, prompt-extraction, exfiltration, tool-steering, hidden-text and encoded-payload families.
